newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy leftist icon arrested on return from exile.
newsitem.headline: Italy leftist icon arrested on return from exile.

text.p: Toni Negri, an icon of the Italian left in the 1970s and alleged ideologue of urban guerrilla groups such as the Red Brigades, returned to Italy voluntarily on Tuesday after 14 years in France and was re-arrested.
He arrived at Rome's Fiumicino airport on a flight from Paris and was immediately driven to Rebibbia prison, where he was first jailed 18 years ago.
With his thin, intense face, mop of curly hair and his firebrand lectures, Negri became a symbol for Italian radicals and students in the turbulent 1970s.
He told reporters on the plane from Paris that he was returning to face jail because he wanted to close a chapter on one of the most violent periods of Italian history.
He was arrested in 1979 in the northern city of Padua, where he was a university professor teaching political science.
Negri was accused of fomenting violence and inciting the 1978 Red Brigades' kidnapping and murder of former Prime Minister Aldo Moro, the country's most notorious political crime.
Negri spent four years in jail and was freed in 1983 after the Radical Party put him forward as a candidate for parliament. He was released from jail because of parliamentary immunity laws.
Parliament lifted his immunity later that year, paving the way for a possible re-arrest. Negri fled on the same day to France, where he resumed his teaching and continued his political activism.
Negri was sentenced in his absence to 12 years on charges of inciting the murder of a police officer. Because of legal technicalities, he is not expected to spend more than four years in jail.
